  PERMITS AND LICENSES COMMITTEE
  MINUTES
  May 28, 2026

A meeting of the Permits and License Committee was conducted at City Hall, Community Room “A” 1st
Floor. On May 28, 2026, at 2:00 p.m.

Roll Call:  Members Present:  Harjinder Singh, Administration Department
  Angel – Leon Martell, Planning Department
  Sgt. Luis Jaramillo, Inglewood Police Department
  Raul Fernandez, Public Works Department
  Emory Ward, Emergency Services Department

  Staff Present:  Destinee Wesley, Deputy City Clerk’s Department
  Shalanda Stringer, Finance Department
  Ruben Rodriguez, Finance Department
  Mayra Perez, Finance Department

Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items
During public comments, any person may address the Permits & License Committee, provided the item is
within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Permits & License Committee.

Christine Rivera asked if there were any persons present who wished to address the Permits & License
Committee on any item on the Agenda.

Christine Rivera reported that there were no public requests to speak.

Approval of the minutes of the meeting held on May 14, 2026

Permit(s):
Item #1:  Produced by 360 on behalf of the City of Inglewood to host The Wood Cup Event on Market
  Street between Florence Ave and Hillcrest Blvd, Public Property, on Friday, June 12, 2026,
  from 2:00 pm to 9:00 p.m. APPROVED CONDITIONALLY SUBJECT TO: Approval for a
  two (2) day event on Market Street between Florence Ave and Hillcrest Blvd. APPROVED:
  IPD (1 LT, 4 SGT, and 26 Officers) & TCO (Staffing required. Meridian barriers required for
  street closures (public works to deploy). These assets will need to remain in place until
  2200 hours due to the watch party event from 1800-2030 hours. Subject to Public Works
  approval for use / closure of the right –of way. Applicant is responsible for crowd control
  and event cleanup. Subject to all applicable IMC regulations. No recommendations needed
  for Fire approval, No recommendations needed for Code Enforment approval,Maintain the
  site at all times, ensuring the site is cleaned correctly immediately at the end of the event;
  Applicant and staff members working this event shall follow all social distancing, protective
  personal hygiene, and face mask wearing safety guidelines set forth by the LA.CO. Health
  Department and CA State health department; and adhere to all State, Federal, LA County,
 Permits & License Committee  May 28, 2026

  and applicable Inglewood Municipal Code rules and regulations, including noise and
  signage. Motion carried unanimously (Activity No. 00427205)

Item #2:  Nora Kelly Reynolds, on behalf of ICEF View Park Prep Elementary, Inc. to host an Annual
  Sports Day Event at Warren Ln, Edward Vincent Jr. Park, City Park, on Monday, June 01,
  2026, from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. APPROVED CONDITIONALLY SUBJECT TO: Approval
  for a one (1) day event at Edward Vincent Park; Subject to Parks and Rec approval for use
  of the park; Applicant is responsible for crowd control and event cleanup. Subject to all
  applicable IMC regulations. Applicant shall staff the event with adequate security and
  personnel for the safety of children and staff attending; female/male security guards shall
  monitor the restrooms used by event attendees; IPD Watch Commander will be notified;
  extra patrol – high visibility will be provided as time permits; manage noise reading; Comply
  with IMC 5-28 and IMC 5-29. Provide a direct point of contact for the person in charge of
  sound and acoustic volume control; No recommendations needed for Fire approval;
  Maintain the site at all times, ensuring it is cleaned correctly immediately at the end of the
  event; Applicant and staff members working this event shall follow all social distancing,
  personal protective hygiene, and face mask-wearing safety guidelines set forth by the
  LA.CO. Health Department and CA State health department; and adhere to all State,
  Federal, LA County, and applicable Inglewood Municipal Code rules and regulations,
  including noise and signage. Motion carried unanimously (Activity No. 00427262)

Item #3:  Jeff Ainsfeld on behalf of RevelXP, to host a SCI Corp World Cup Tailgate Event at 714
  East Manchester Blvd, Parking Lot, Private Property, on Friday, June 12, 2026, from 4:00
  p.m. to 9:30 p.m. APPROVED CONDITIONALLY SUBJECT TO: Applicant approved for
  a one (1) day event within private parking lot; applicant responsible for crowd control, event
  clean up, and all applicabe measures; Approved Conditionally; Applicant shall staff this
  event with a minimum three (3) professional / licensed security guards for the safety
  of attendees. NO alcohol sales without an approved ABC one day permit which
  should be submitted by a licensed caterer, catering this event. This event should
  only be open to pre-paid / invitation persons, CLOSED to the general public. Adhere
  to all local, state, federal laws in addition to the terms & conditions of the permit
  issued for this event. Adhere to IMC 12-16.9 Tailgating Regulations; No
  Recommendations needed for Fire approval; maintain the site at all times, ensuring it is
  cleaned properly immediately upon the end of the event. Applicant and staff members
  working this event shall follow all social distancing, personal protective hygiene, and face
  mask-wearing safety guidelines set forth by the LA.CO. Health Department and CA State
  health department; and adhere to all State, Federal, LA County, and applicable Inglewood
  Municipal Code rules and regulations, including noise and signage. Motion carried
  unanimously (Activity No. 00427240)

Item #4:  Rikki Ferrell on behalf of Greater New Bethel Baptist Church to operate as a Parking Lot
  at 1201 S. Flower St. APPROVED CONDITIONALL SUBJECT TO THE FOLLOWING
  STIPULATIONS:Payment of annual business license and tax fees, an expired or lapsed
  license for more than six month will negatively impact your license renewal;Remittances of
  Parking Tax by the 20th of each month following collection;Approval for Special Event
  Parking Forum events only;Special Event Parking must not start before 6 pm Monday
  through Friday;On Site business must be closed 1 hour before Event Parking starts.Parking
  attendant or security guards must be on site during event parking at all times;Ensure safe
  pedestrian and vehicular circulation on/off site and;No Tailgating;Adhere to all State,
  Federal and Inglewood Municipal Code rules and regulations, including noise and
  signage.Failure to comply with any of the aforementioned will result in revocation of
  your business license and any future license application requests. Motion carried
  unanimously (Activity No. 00427247)

New Tobacco Retailer License Renewal Request (s):

Item #7:  Ashley Lopez on behalf of Moxie Market LLC to operate as a tobacco Retailer at 3535 W.
  Imperial Hwy This Business License has been APPROVED with the following
  condition set forth by the Permits and Licenses Committee:Must adhere to all City of
  Inglewood Municipal Codes (IMC), specifically; CHAPTER 8: Article 8. REGULATIONS
  FOR BUSINESSES ENGAGED IN THE SALE OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS;Must adhere
  to all State and Federal Rules and Regulations; Retail area not exceed 32 Square Feet or
  25% of total retail floor area Sales or display of single cigarettes is strictly prohibited; Sales
  of Flavored E-Cigarettes , Flavored Vapes ,Flavored E-juice, Flavored Pods, Flavored
  Cartridges, Menthol Cigarettes; Flavored little Cigars, Flavored Cigarillos, Flavored
  Smokeless Tobacco Products, Flavored Blunts Wraps, Flavored loose-leaf roll-your-own
  Tobacco, Flavored Tobacco rolling papers, Tobacco Product Flavored Enhancers are
  Strictly Prohibited;Tobacco or smoke shop retailers are required to immediately
  remove any Kratom related products, including natural Kratom and any products
  containing 7-OH, from store shelves and cease all sales;Sales of tobacco, hookah,
  vapor and e-cigarette products to minors, under age 21 is strictly prohibited; Persons
  purchasing tobacco or any related tobacco products shall have a valid government-issued
  identification on their person at all times to enforce laws restricting underage access to
  tobacco use, including hookah products; Sales or display of any type of weapons, i.e.,
  clubs, swords, knives, pepper spray, Taser/Stun guns is strictly prohibited;Tobacco Retailer
  business owners and/or new applicants or their designees are subject to random Permits
  & Licenses establishment inspections at any time of the day or night by any Police or Code
  Enforcement Officers, purpose of random inspections is to enforce business
  establishments to adhere to the regulations set forth by the City of Inglewood for
  Community Public Health & Safety;California State Board of Equalization Tobacco
  Retailers license must be current;Approval for retail sales of tobacco products within
  existing business ONLY;NO sales of tobacco (including vaporized / hookah products) to
  minors / underage persons. All persons purchasing tobacco or any related tobacco
  products SHALL have valid ID on their person at all times to ensure the restriction of
  underage tobacco use, including hookah products;Submit all state tobacco renewal
  certificates if applicable;NO loitering of persons outside of the location;NO LOITERING /
  PANHANDLING SIGNS MUST BE POSTED and visible to outside of the business. Proof
  of signage posted by applicant shall be submitted to finance (i.e. photo of signage); The
  following is not allowed: the “sales of Whippets are small cylinders of nitrous oxide”, the
  use of or illegal sales or cultivation of marijuana/cannabis products, any regulated cannabis
  products, any use or possession of illegal or unauthorized narcotics, narcotic paraphernalia
  per H&S11364.5 - i.e.; any pipes specifically used to ingest illegal narcotics, this would also
  include glass cylindrical, tube or bubble shaped pipes used specifically to smoke / ingest
  illegal narcotics. Sales of Tobacco pipes are acceptable; Applicant and employees are
  expected to be active participants in calling/notifying police for police related, unusual,
  illegal, and/or activity that may necessitate a police response or response from other city
  government services (i.e. Code Enforcement, Planning, Finance, Public Works, Fire Dept.,
  Etc.);Applicant and employees are expected to be active participants in calling/notifying
